originalTitle: Nigeria's president launches re-election manifesto but can he regain voters' trust?
title: Nigeria's Big News: The President's Promises!
content:
Hello from Nigeria!

Hi everyone! It's your friend, the kid-friendly news reporter, coming to you live from the amazing continent of Africa! Today, we're going on a special adventure to a very big and beautiful country called Nigeria. Can you say Nigeria? It's right here in Africa! Did you know that Nigeria has so many friendly people? It's like a giant family with lots of brothers, sisters, and cousins! In every country, there's a very important person called the President. The President is like the head of a big family, helping everyone in the country. He makes sure things run smoothly and tries to make life good for all the people, especially kids like you!

What is a President?

Imagine your school principal, but for a whole country! That's a bit like what a President does. The President helps decide about schools, hospitals, and even roads. He wants everyone to be safe and happy. It's a very big job, and it needs a lot of thinking and caring. Did you know that different countries have different leaders? But many countries in Africa, like Nigeria, have a President!

A Special Book of Promises!

Now, something exciting happened in Nigeria! The President, whose name is Bola Ahmed Tinubu, did something special. He showed everyone a special book. It's not a storybook, but a book full of promises! We call this a "manifesto." Think of it like when you promise your friend you'll share your toys, or when your parents promise you a special treat if you help clean up. This book has all the things the President hopes to do if he gets to be President again. It's like a plan for the future! Did you know that leaders usually make promises before grown-ups vote for them? It helps people decide who they want to lead.

What Kinds of Promises?

So, what kind of promises are in this special book? They are promises to make Nigeria a better place for everyone. Maybe promises for better schools, so kids can learn even more cool stuff! Imagine new books and fun playgrounds. Perhaps promises for better hospitals, so when someone feels sick, they can get help quickly and feel better soon. There might be promises for yummy food for everyone, so no one is hungry. And promises for safe homes and safe streets, so everyone can play and live without worries. Did you know that clean water is super important? Promises might include making sure everyone has clean water to drink and wash with!

Wanting to Be President Again

Our President, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, wants to keep doing his important job. He wants to be President for another turn. This is called "re-election." It means he is asking the grown-ups in Nigeria to choose him again when they vote. He believes he can do a great job and wants to continue helping Nigeria grow stronger and happier. Did you know that most Presidents serve for a few years and then can ask to be re-elected?

Why Do People Need to Trust Leaders?

This is a super important part! Grown-ups in Nigeria are thinking about something called "trust." What is trust? It's when you believe someone will do what they say they will do. Imagine if your friend promised to play with you, but then they didn't. You might feel a little sad and not trust their promises so much next time, right? It's the same for a President. People want to trust that the President will keep his promises and work hard for them. If people trust their leader, they feel happy and safe. They know things will get better. Did you know that trust makes everything work better? Like trusting your teacher to teach you new things, or your parents to take care of you.

Making Things Even Better!

Some wise people, who think a lot about how countries work, are saying something important. They say that for people to truly feel things are getting much, much better, the changes need to be really big. They call these big changes "reforms" or "improvements." It's like when you try to tidy your room. You can just put one toy away, or you can make a big change and clean everything and make it sparkle! They hope the President's plans will be like making the whole room sparkle, not just one small corner. Did you know that when a country makes big improvements, it means better lives for everyone, from grandmas and grandpas to little babies?

Wise People Are Talking

Who are these "wise people"? They are smart grown-ups called "analysts." Analysts study how countries work, how money moves, and how people feel. They look at the President's promises and think about what might happen. They share their ideas. They are like super-smart detectives, trying to figure out the best way forward for Nigeria. Did you know that these analysts help leaders and regular people understand big ideas?

It's Like Promises to Your Friends!

Let's think about your own promises. If you promise to help your mom or dad, and you do it, they trust you more. Right? If the President promises better roads and then the roads really get better, people will feel happy and trust him more. It’s about seeing the promises turn into real, helpful things in everyday life. Did you know that keeping promises is a great way to show you care and build strong friendships?

Working Together for a Happy Nigeria

So, the President has made his promises in his special book. Now, everyone in Nigeria, from the President to every single family, hopes that these promises can make a really big difference. They hope for a Nigeria where every child can go to a good school, where everyone is safe, and where families are happy and healthy. It takes everyone working together to make a country great. The President leads, and the people support by working hard too. Did you know that when people work together, amazing things can happen? Just like when you and your friends work together to build a tall tower of blocks! We will all watch to see how these big promises help Nigeria shine even brighter! That’s all from your kid-friendly reporter for today! Bye for now!
summary: Nigeria's President has made new promises to the people to make their country better and hopes they will trust him to lead again.
whyMatters: This is important because when leaders keep their promises, people feel safe and happy, and the country can grow strong for everyone.

originalTitle: Eswatini gives illegal foreign businesses 12 months to leave
title: Helping Our Local Shops Shine in Eswatini!
content:
Hello, Super Reporters!

Hello, super friends! It's your kid-friendly news reporter, here from the heart of Africa! Today, we're going on an exciting adventure to a special country called Eswatini. Can you say E-swa-tini? Great job! It's a beautiful place with friendly people and lots of interesting things happening. We're going to talk about something important that will help many families and their shops right there in Eswatini. Get ready to learn and be amazed!

What's This Big News About?

Imagine you have a favorite toy, and you want everyone to play fair with it. Well, countries have rules too, just like in your games! The grown-ups who help run Eswatini, called the government, have made a new rule. This rule is about shops. You know, places where you buy yummy snacks, clothes, or even pretty crafts. Some shops in Eswatini are owned by people from other countries. That's okay! But just like when you visit a friend's house, you need to follow their rules. Some of these shops might not have been following all the rules. So, the government is kindly telling them, 'Hey, please make sure you follow our rules, or you might need to find a new place to sell things.' They are giving these shops about a year – that's 12 whole months – to get everything right or to move. It's all about making things fair for everyone!

What Does "Foreign" Mean?

Sometimes, we hear big words like 'foreign'. Don't worry, it's easy! Imagine your friend comes to visit you from another town. Your friend is 'foreign' to your town, but they are still a person, just like you! It's the same with shops. A 'foreign business' just means a shop or a company that is owned by someone who comes from a different country than Eswatini. These people might have come from a country far, far away, or even a country very close by. They bring different things and ideas, which can be fun! But every country has its own special way of doing things, especially for shops.

Why Do We Need Rules for Shops?

Think about your classroom. You have rules, right? Like raising your hand or sharing toys. These rules help everyone get along and make sure things are fair. It's the same for shops! Rules, or 'laws' as grown-ups call them, help make sure that all shops are safe, sell good things, and treat their workers fairly. When everyone follows the rules, it helps the whole country grow strong and happy. If some shops don't follow the rules, it can make it harder for other shops, especially the ones owned by people who live right there in Eswatini, to do well. **Did You Know?** Eswatini used to be called Swaziland! It's one of the smallest countries in Africa, but it's full of big hearts and beautiful traditions!

Shops in Our Villages and Countryside

Many of these shops that need to follow new rules are in places called 'rural areas'. This is a fancy word for villages, small towns, and the countryside, far away from the big cities. In these places, local shops are super important! Imagine your grandma selling fresh fruits and vegetables she grew in her garden, or your uncle making beautiful woven baskets. These are local businesses, and they help their families and neighbors. When new shops come into these quiet villages, it's great sometimes because they bring new things. But if they don't follow the rules, or if there are too many of them, it can make it hard for grandma or uncle to sell their wonderful things. The government wants to make sure that the local people in these villages have the best chance to make a living and help their communities grow. **Did You Know?** Local shops often sell unique things that are made right there in Eswatini, like delicious local honey or colorful handcrafted jewelry! Buying from them helps local families directly.

Helping Our Local Heroes

This new rule is like giving a high-five to all the local heroes who own shops in Eswatini! When local people own shops and businesses, the money they earn often stays right in their community. They use it to buy food from other local farmers, send their kids to school, or build a better home. This helps the whole village get stronger! It means more jobs for local people, more delicious food from local farms, and more wonderful things made by local artists. The government hopes this new rule will help these local shops shine even brighter and make Eswatini an even happier place for everyone who lives there.

What Happens Next?

So, what happens now? The government isn't saying 'Poof! You're gone tomorrow!' They are being very kind and giving these shops 12 months, which is one whole year. This gives them lots of time to understand the rules, get all their papers in order, or decide if they need to move. It's a big change, but it's a good change, like planting a seed that will grow into a strong, beautiful tree. It helps everyone play fair and makes sure that Eswatini's own people have great opportunities to run successful shops. Everyone wants to see Eswatini's villages and towns flourish! **Did You Know?** In many African countries, marketplaces are bustling and colorful places where people buy and sell goods. They are like giant outdoor supermarkets where you can find everything from clothes to spices!

Time to Celebrate Fairness!

So there you have it, brave reporters! Big news from Eswatini, all about helping local shops and making sure everyone plays by the rules. It's a wonderful way to help communities grow strong and happy. Remember, rules are there to keep things fair and help everyone succeed! Keep exploring and learning about our amazing continent, Africa!
summary: Eswatini is helping its local shops by asking businesses from other countries to follow rules or move, giving them one year to do so.
whyMatters: This helps local people in Eswatini keep their shops, earn money, and make their villages stronger and happier.

originalTitle: Israel strikes intensive care at Gaza’s Nasser Hospital
title: Helpers in Hospitals: A Sad Story from Far Away
content:
Hello, Little Explorers!

Hello, my little explorers and curious minds! Your friend, the news reporter from Africa, is here with some news from a place far, far away. Today, we're going to talk about something very important: hospitals! Do you know what a hospital is? It's a very special building where amazing doctors and kind nurses work very hard. They help people who are sick or hurt get better. Sometimes, tiny new babies are born there! Hospitals are places of hope, healing, and lots of caring. Imagine a big, friendly building full of beds, special machines, and people in white coats and colourful uniforms. That’s a hospital! It’s where you go if you fall and scrape your knee very badly, or if you have a tummy ache that won't go away. Hospitals should always be safe places, full of calm and kindness, where everyone can feel protected. Doctors give medicine, nurses give hugs, and everyone works together like a big, caring family.

A Special Hospital in Gaza

Now, let's talk about a place called Gaza. It's a town very, very far from us, across the big blue ocean. In Gaza, there is a big hospital called Nasser Hospital. It's just like the hospitals we know, full of doctors and nurses who work hard to help people. They have special rooms for people who are very, very sick and need extra care, maybe because they are very old or very young, or had a big accident. These rooms are called 'intensive care' rooms, which means they are for people who need lots and lots of attention all the time to get better. One day, something very, very sad happened at Nasser Hospital. There was a big noise, and a part of the hospital got hurt. It was like someone threw a big, hard rock at a very important house. The place where the very sick people were getting special care was hit. It was a very scary moment for everyone there – the patients, the doctors, the nurses, and all the kind helpers. Did you know? Hospitals have special rooms for different things. Some rooms are for broken bones, some for tummy aches, and some for having babies! They even have special kitchens to cook healthy food for everyone.

Brave Helpers All Around

When this sad thing happened, some grown-ups who were helping others were hurt very badly. Some of these brave helpers, who worked so hard to keep people safe and healthy, lost their lives. This made many, many people very sad, especially their families and friends. They were heroes, doing their best to help everyone, even when things were difficult and scary around them. Imagine a superhero, but instead of a cape, they wear a doctor's coat or a nurse's uniform, or a uniform like a firefighter! In Gaza, there are also special helpers called Civil Defence. Think of them like super brave firefighters and rescuers. When there's a big problem, like a building getting hurt, they rush in to help. They try to find people who need help, clean up the mess, and make sure everyone is as safe as possible. They are always ready to lend a hand, no matter how scary the situation might be. These Civil Defence people were also helping at Nasser Hospital after the sad event. Did you know? Doctors and nurses often work very long hours, sometimes even through the night, to make sure everyone is cared for. They are very dedicated!

Why Hospitals Must Be Safe

Hospitals are places of peace and healing. They should always be safe, no matter what. Everyone in the world agrees that doctors, nurses, and all the kind helpers in hospitals should be able to do their important jobs without worrying about big noises or dangerous things happening. Sick people, little babies, and old grandmas need a quiet, safe place to get better. When a hospital is hurt, it makes it harder for sick people to get the help they need, and it makes all the brave helpers very sad and worried. Imagine if your school or your home suddenly became unsafe. That's how it feels when a hospital, a place meant to protect and heal, gets hurt. It means that the people who need medicine, who need a comforting hand, or who need a safe place to rest, might not get it. That's why we always hope and wish for hospitals everywhere to be safe and peaceful. Did you know? There are hospitals for animals too! They are called veterinary hospitals, and doctors there are called veterinarians. They help our furry and feathered friends when they are sick.

What Can We Do?

When we hear sad news like this from far away, it's okay to feel a little bit sad or worried. But remember, there are always good people trying to help. We can send our kind thoughts to the children and grown-ups in Gaza. We can hope that everyone who was hurt at Nasser Hospital gets better very, very soon. And we can remember to always be kind to everyone around us, because kindness is a superpower that can make the world a better place. Even though we are far away, we can still learn from stories like this. We can learn how important it is for everyone to work together. We can learn to appreciate the brave doctors, nurses, and all the helpers in our own communities. We can promise to be good friends, help our families, and always look out for each other. Because when we are kind and helpful, we are building a world where everyone can feel safe and loved. Did you know? In many African countries, people walk for many hours to get to a hospital to see a doctor. That's why building more hospitals is so important! Let’s all wish for peace and safety for Nasser Hospital and for all hospitals around the world. Let’s remember the brave helpers and hope for a brighter, safer future for everyone. Thank you for listening, my little explorers!
summary: A sad incident happened at Nasser Hospital in Gaza, where part of the hospital was damaged and some brave helpers were hurt very badly, reminding us that hospitals should always be safe places for everyone to heal.
whyMatters: This is important because hospitals are safe places where doctors and nurses help sick and hurt people, and they should always be protected so everyone can get the care they need.

originalTitle: Former Italian Red Brigades member escapes house arrest in Argentina
title: A Grown-Up Climbs Down a Building!
content:
Hello, Super Reporters!

Hi everyone! It's your kid-friendly news reporter here, coming to you all the way from sunny Africa! I have a really interesting story to tell you today, and it's about a grown-up who did something quite surprising far, far away.

A Grown-Up Who Couldn't Stay Home

Imagine you are told you have to stay in your room. Maybe you had a little timeout, or you needed to finish your homework. Well, a grown-up named Mr. Bertulazzi (we say it like: Ber-too-LAHT-see) was told he had to stay in his house. This is called 'house arrest'. It means grown-ups who did something wrong in the past are asked to stay home so that special helpers, called 'authorities', can keep an eye on them. Mr. Bertulazzi was supposed to stay inside his apartment. An apartment is like a home inside a very big building with many other homes. But guess what? He didn't! He found a very clever way to leave, even though he wasn't supposed to. He snuck away!

Climbing Down a Tall Building!

This happened in a place called Argentina. It's a country very far away from Africa, across a big, blue ocean! Argentina is in a part of the world called South America. Mr. Bertulazzi lived in a tall, tall building in Argentina. He was on the fifth floor! Can you imagine how high that is? It's like going up five big sets of stairs! To get down from such a high place, he didn't use the stairs or an elevator. No! He used a special rope and something called a 'harness'. A harness is like a super-safe belt that goes around your body and keeps climbers from falling. It helps them move up and down safely. He used these tools to climb down, down, down, from the fifth floor all the way to the ground! It was like something you might see in a movie, but this was real! He wanted to leave his house arrest, and he used his rope and harness to do it. The people watching him, the authorities, were very surprised when they found he was gone!

Why Was He on House Arrest?

Now, you might be wondering, why was Mr. Bertulazzi told to stay home in the first place? Well, a long, long time ago, when he was much younger, he was part of a group of people who did some things that were not good. They made people sad and sometimes scared. So, the grown-ups who make sure everyone is safe, the 'authorities', decided he needed to be watched. House arrest is a way to make sure people who did wrong things stay safe and don't do anything else bad. It’s like a very big timeout for grown-ups. It helps everyone remember that rules are important for a happy and safe community. The authorities wanted to make sure he was not causing any more trouble.

Did You Know?

**Did you know?** Argentina is famous for a beautiful dance called Tango! It's also known for having lots of cows and yummy steaks. Argentina is a country with big mountains and wide open spaces, very different from many parts of Africa where we have our own special animals and dances! **Did you know?** Ropes have been used by people for thousands of years! People use ropes for climbing, pulling heavy things, tying boats, and even for fun sports like jumping rope! But climbing down a building, especially a tall one, needs lots of practice and safety gear. Usually, only brave firefighters or special builders do something like that!

What Happens Next?

Because Mr. Bertulazzi left when he wasn't supposed to, the authorities in Argentina are now looking for him. They want to find him to make sure he is safe and that he follows the rules. It's their job to keep everyone in the country safe, and that means making sure people who are on house arrest stay where they are supposed to be. Finding someone who has gone missing is a very important job for the police and other helpers. They will use all their tools and smart ideas to figure out where Mr. Bertulazzi might have gone. They will search carefully, asking questions and looking for clues, just like super detectives!

Why This Story Matters

This story reminds us that rules are important for everyone, no matter if you're a kid or a grown-up. Rules help keep us safe and help us live together happily. When someone doesn't follow the rules, it can make things tricky, and the grown-ups in charge need to work hard to make things right again. It’s also important to remember that 'authorities' – like police officers and other community helpers – are there to help us. They work hard to make sure our communities are safe places for everyone to play and grow. They are like big brothers and sisters who watch out for everyone. So, always remember to listen to your parents and teachers, and follow the rules! It helps make the world a happier and safer place for all of us, from Africa to Argentina and everywhere in between! That's all for today from your kid reporter! See you next time!
summary: A grown-up named Mr. Bertulazzi, who was supposed to stay at home in Argentina because he broke rules a long time ago, climbed down a tall building using a rope to escape, and now authorities are looking for him.
whyMatters: It's important for everyone to follow rules to keep communities safe, and this story shows what happens when grown-ups don't follow them, making special helpers (authorities) work to find them.

originalTitle: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike
title: People in a Faraway Land Ask for Fair Homes and Prices!
content:
Hello, super kids of Africa! Your friendly news reporter is here with an exciting story from far, far away. Today, we're going to talk about something important that happened in a beautiful country called Spain. It’s a country that is very far from us, across the big, blue ocean!

What Happened in Spain?

Imagine if many, many grown-ups decided to take a day off from work all at the same time. Not because it was a holiday, but because they wanted to tell their leaders something very important! That's what happened in a big city in Spain called Barcelona. Tens of thousands of people, that means so many people you can't even count them all with your fingers and toes, gathered together. They walked in the streets and held up signs. They wanted everyone to know they were unhappy about some things. Did you know? Spain is famous for its delicious food like paella and churros, and its amazing football teams! It's a country full of sunshine, just like many places here in Africa.

What is a 'Strike'?

When many people stop working together to show they are unhappy about something, we call it a 'strike'. It's like when you and your friends all agree to say 'NO!' to something you don't like, but for grown-ups and their jobs. The grown-ups in Spain were on strike because they wanted their voices to be heard. They wanted to make things better for everyone. A strike is a way for people to show how strongly they feel about something. Did you know? People have been going on strike for hundreds of years! It's a very old way for workers to ask for fair treatment and better lives.

Why Were They Upset? Homes!

One big reason these grown-ups were upset was about homes. Everyone needs a safe, warm, and happy place to live, right? A home where you can play, eat yummy food, and sleep soundly. But in Spain, many people are finding it very, very hard to find a good home. Or, the homes they find are too expensive for them to rent or buy. Imagine wanting a cosy bed but not being able to find one that your parents can afford. That's a sad feeling! These people want to make sure everyone has a fair chance to live in a nice house. They believe that having a good home is a very important right for all families. A happy home makes happy families, and happy families make a happy country. Did you know? Some homes in Spain are very old and beautiful, with colourful tiles and pretty balconies! But even old homes need to be safe and affordable for people to live in.

Why Were They Upset? Things Cost Too Much!

Another big reason for the strike was that things cost too much money. This is called the 'high cost of living'. Imagine your favourite snack or your school uniform suddenly becoming super, super expensive. It means that simple things like food, clothes, and even the electricity to light up your home are becoming very expensive. Grown-ups work hard to earn money, but if everything costs too much, their money doesn't go very far. It can be very worrying for parents to think about how they will buy food for their children or pay for the electricity bill. They want prices to be fair so that their families can live comfortably without always worrying about money. They want to be able to buy healthy food and have enough money left over for other important things, like going to school or seeing a doctor if they are sick. Fair prices help everyone live better lives. Did you know? In some parts of the world, people use different money! In Spain, they use money called 'Euros'. It looks a bit different from the money we use here in Africa.

People Work Together: Unions!

So, who asked all these people to go on strike? It was groups called 'unions'. Think of a union like a big club for workers. These clubs help workers by talking to the bosses and leaders about things that are important to them. When many people join a union, their voice becomes much, much stronger than if they just complained alone. The unions in Spain asked everyone to join together. They wanted to show the government how many people were unhappy and needed help with homes and prices. It's like teamwork to solve a big problem! Did you know? Unions try to make sure that grown-ups have safe places to work, get paid fairly, and have enough time off to rest. They are like protectors for workers!

How Do They Show They Are Unhappy?

Most of the time, when people go on strike, they walk together peacefully. They carry colourful signs with words that say what they want. They might sing songs or chant slogans to share their message loudly. Sometimes, when so many people are very, very upset and want to be heard, things can get a little bit loud or messy. But mostly, people just want to show how much they care about making their country a better place for everyone. Their main goal is for the leaders to listen to them and make changes so that homes are easier to find and prices are fair. They want a brighter future for their children, just like your parents want for you! Did you know? People marching together is called a 'protest'. It's a way for many people to share their feelings and ask for change without hurting anyone.

Why Does This Matter to Us?

Even though Spain is far away, this story shows us that people everywhere want the same basic things: a safe home, enough food, and a fair chance to live a good life. It teaches us about being brave and using our voices to ask for what is fair. It reminds us that working together, like the unions did, can make a big difference. So, remember, kids: whether it's in Spain or right here in Africa, everyone deserves to be happy and to have a safe home and enough food. Keep learning, keep asking questions, and always be kind! This is your friendly African news reporter, signing off! See you next time for more exciting news!
summary: Tens of thousands of people in Spain went on strike to tell their leaders they are unhappy about the high cost of homes and everyday things like food and clothes.
whyMatters: This story matters because it shows that grown-ups everywhere want fair homes and fair prices for important things, and that working together can help them make their voices heard for a better life.
